panels.question: How do stationary mean lattice-current components decay with temperature, including trajectory-level uncertainty?
panels.uncertainty_definition: trajectory-level 95% intervals; low-T N=500 and pooled high-T N=1000 as declared in caption

panels.question: Does the full two-component stationary mean current remain distinguishable from zero at high temperature?
How does weak directional cycle bias compare with preservation of the exact deterministic target winding?

caption: Figure 6. Stationary thermal hierarchy from trajectory-level inference. (a) Mean lattice-coordinate currents <u> and <v> after 60 burn cycles and 100 measured cycles. The low-temperature full series uses N=500 trajectories per T*, while T*=0.50-0.70 uses the pooled two-seed N=1000 estimates; error bars are trajectory-level 95% intervals. (b) High-temperature Hotelling zero-current rejection ratio for the pooled two-seed ensembles; values above one reject the zero-current vector under the declared test and are not interpreted as a thermal critical scale. (c) The negative-v cycle probability approaches one-half while the exact deterministic target-winding probability remains near 1% in the high-temperature band, separating weak directed drift from preservation of the deterministic mode identity.
